claims.description: The uint64Slice sorting adapter must expose numeric ascending order and exchange indexed values without changing the multiset of reported indexes used by commitment calculation.

scope.description: Supporting sorting adapter consumed by recalculate.
assumptions: The sorting caller supplies valid slice indexes.
excluded: Correctness of the standard-library sorting algorithm
Truth or durability of reported progress

pending: Included as a supporting dependency; not added to U_commit's checked obligations.

grounding.derivation: The existing B_recalculate mapping identifies sorted rank selection as the consumer. The newly read adapter returns slice length, compares values using numeric less-than, and swaps indexed values. Ascending order and value preservation are a derived consumer requirement, not a normative conclusion established merely by observing these implementations.
grounding.applicability: Applies to the uint64Slice adapter used by the existing commitment calculation. Its implementation must be included as supporting behavior without assuming this candidate obligation holds.
unresolved: No separate executable check of this supporting obligation is supplied.
The standard-library sorting implementation is outside the supplied material.
alternatives: Another rank-selection implementation could satisfy the consumer requirement, but no replacement mechanism is established by the supplied graph.

associations.rationale: Provides the length, numeric comparator and swap operations consumed when recalculate sorts reported indexes.

bindings.description: Declares the slice adapter and its Len, Less and Swap methods. Less uses p[i] < p[j]; Swap exchanges the two elements.
pending: Reading the adapter does not independently validate the sorting caller or the complete rank calculation.

associations.rationale: Supplies the notification behavior called by recalculate at its advancement boundary; notification delivery is not a checked obligation.

bindings.description: Attempts a channel send in a select with a default branch. It does not wait for a receiver when sending cannot proceed; successful delivery is not guaranteed.
pending: Channel allocation, ownership and closure rules are not supplied.
A closed channel can panic on send; the helper's default branch does not establish safety against closure.
Nonblocking notification does not establish absence of scheduler interleaving or downstream consumption.

associations.rationale: Provides the configuration input schema and server identity declarations needed to construct inputs to newCommitment and setConfiguration.

bindings.description: Declares Configuration.Servers and the adjacent Server, ServerID and ServerAddress input types. Comments describe persistent server identity and configurations with no repeated server entries; these declarations do not enforce either condition.
pending: Input declarations do not establish configuration-transition legality or runtime validation.
The documented lifetime of ServerID does not imply that progress survives voter removal and readdition.

associations.rationale: Identifies the actual suffrage constants used when constructing voter and nonvoter inputs for the commitment component.

bindings.description: Declares ServerSuffrage and Voter, Nonvoter and Staging constants. The comments assign commitment participation to Voter and describe Nonvoter and Staging as excluded from commitment participation.
pending: The declaration does not establish which suffrage transitions callers may legally submit.

relations.rationale: The existing sorted-rank commitment calculation depends on the adapter supplying numeric ascending order without losing or fabricating reported values.
pending: The supporting obligation is not separately checked by U_commit.
This dependency establishes neither sufficient replication support nor notification delivery.

grounding.derivation: B_recalculate's existing mapping selects the majority threshold from sorted reported indexes. The newly supplied uint64Slice declaration implements the adapter that determines ordering and element exchange. Incorrect adapter behavior could invalidate that numerical interpretation.
grounding.applicability: A directed consumer-to-support dependency for the existing rank-selection mechanism. It permits U_commit to include the actual adapter as supporting behavior without adding its obligation to checked coverage.
unresolved: The dependency is grounded in the existing commitment mapping and newly read helper; it is not an executable validation result.
Standard-library sorting remains an external runtime dependency.
alternatives: A different selection mechanism could avoid this adapter dependency, but none is established for the mapped implementation.

audit_question.question: Can any bounded sequence of match reports and voter-map replacements cause this commitment instance to advance without a strict majority of its current reported indexes or before startIndex, or cause stored progress to decrease?
audit_question.importance: The resulting index authorizes downstream command application. The component is small enough to investigate without deterministic network scheduling.

points.question: Across one instance's ordered operations, does each advancement have sufficient current reported support and satisfy the threshold while preserving monotonic progress?
unknowns: Operation order must be correlated by commitment-instance identity and ServerID; no global rounds are established.
Arbitrary setter sequences establish component behavior, not necessarily legal cluster histories.

audit_question.trigger_rationale: Selected from the documented Apply dependency and the fully supplied commitment implementation; no historical defect is needed.

code_uses.rationale: Implements progress admission and monotonic updates.

unverified: Protocol eligibility of each configuration change

code_uses.rationale: Produces the index advances checked locally.
Includes the actual sorting adapter through the directed dependency from O_commit. Its method bodies supply behavior; its supporting obligation is not assumed or counted as checked.

Includes the actual nonblocking send attempt at recalculate's notification boundary. The default branch prevents waiting for a receiver but does not guarantee delivery or make the surrounding operation globally atomic.
unverified: Notification channel lifecycle and closure legality

code_uses.rationale: Supplies actual configuration and server field types for constructing package-level component inputs. Documented identity and uniqueness expectations do not establish enforcement or legal setter histories.
Supplies declared suffrage values for voter-map construction and replacement, without adding configuration correctness to checked coverage.
unverified: Eligibility of suffrage changes in actual cluster histories

scope.description: Rank 1: bounded component investigation of commitment arithmetic and state transitions.
assumptions: Use serialized component operations or the actual mutex discipline.

units.rationale: Highest-ranked feasible unit because its implementation is completely supplied, its responsibility directly supports Apply, and ordinary package tests can observe its state transitions. Any local result leaves report soundness and global configuration history unresolved.

rationale: Propose a dependency-only continuation for controller ScopeUpdate assessment. The only changed existing fields are U_commit.binding_ids, U_commit.relation_ids and U_commit.code_uses. Add the read sorting adapter, notification helper and configuration declarations while preserving existing claims, checked obligations, audit question, coverage meaning and scope. No existing semantic dispute is resolved by these additions.
gaps: U_commit's question and coverage point still contain disputed wording about unconditional progress monotonicity. Exploratory checking must retain O_commit's narrower restriction on match reports and allow progress reset after voter removal and readdition. Revising the existing wording requires separate semantic assessment.
All existing semantic-readiness disputes remain unresolved; this patch supplies dependencies and does not authorize confirmation of an implementation defect.

The notification helper establishes a nonblocking attempt, not guaranteed delivery. Production channel creation, closure and consumption are unread; channel-closure fault applicability cannot be inferred.
Configuration declarations enable source-grounded input construction but do not establish legal membership histories, caller validation or persistent identity enforcement.
O_commit_sort_adapter is supporting context and remains outside U_commit's checked obligations. Standard-library sorting behavior remains an external runtime dependency.
Report durability and correlation, startIndex initialization, commitment-to-FSM handoff and historical configuration support remain unresolved. Snapshot investigation remains deferred.
No executable trace, calibration or implementation reproduction evidence is supplied by this patch.
